recognize_zh: 箭頭所指的細胞一端伸出一條細胞質尾巴（uropod），形狀像手持鏡子（hand mirror cells），核質比高、染色質細緻；此形態可見於急性白血病（淋巴芽細胞較常見），但不具譜系特異性。
features: Immature mononuclear cells with high N:C ratio and finely granular chromatin
Unipolar cytoplasmic projection (uropod) producing a hand-mirror shape (arrows)
Scant basophilic cytoplasm concentrated in the tail region
Several other cells with similar polarized cytoplasm; one small cell with dense chromatin
Background red cells with an erythrocyte containing small refractile inclusions
describe_en: Smear shows several immature mononuclear cells with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios and finely granular chromatin. Many display a unipolar tail of basophilic cytoplasm (uropod), imparting a hand-mirror configuration, as highlighted by the arrows. Cytoplasmic granules and Auer rods are not seen. Findings are consistent with hand mirror cells, a nonspecific morphologic variant most often seen in acute lymphoblastic leukemia but also in other acute leukemias; lineage requires flow cytometry.

ddx.vs: Crush artifact produces smeared, streaming nuclear chromatin without an intact nucleus and discrete cytoplasmic tail.
Megakaryoblasts show multiple peripheral blebs rather than a single uropod, and are CD41/CD61 positive.
Plasma cells have an eccentric nucleus with clumped chromatin and perinuclear hof, and more abundant uniformly blue cytoplasm.
